answer: Mirror-Grove Registration. Each new identity plants a grove slot whose state must match a marble drawn from a shared public pool; duplicates collide because two slots claiming one marble expose a mismatched velocity trace in the velvet log. The rule: every identity must advance its marble through a unique path, so a clone either forks the trace visibly or stalls. An attacker pays one marble draw plus the compute to sustain a divergent trace per clone, and any divergence is published, making duplication self-revealing.
